rationale: After the ICD-11 phase-classification block, this item checks whether learners can correctly map specific disorders to the phase of the sexual response cycle they disrupt — the core conceptual framework of the section.

After the organic-versus-psychogenic aetiology block, this item probes whether learners can critically evaluate a commonly cited but oversimplified clinical distinction, pushing them beyond recall to analysis.

After the management block covering pharmacological, psychological, and couple-based interventions, this item requires learners to select the most appropriate first-line combination for a typical clinical presentation, integrating the multimodal approach described.

After the block on the Indian legal framework for LGBTQA+ rights, this item checks accurate recall of landmark judicial decisions and statutes — precise dates and holdings matter for clinical and medicolegal practice.

After the ICD-11 declassification block, this item tests a nuanced but clinically critical distinction: ICD-11 removed homosexuality as a disorder decades ago (ICD-10 already did this), but also moved gender incongruence OUT of the mental disorders chapter — these are two separate reclassification events that learners often conflate.

After the block on distinguishing minority stress from psychopathology, this item presents a clinical vignette requiring learners to apply the minority stress model to a realistic patient encounter — the most practically important skill taught in this SDL.
